summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with HCV-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and a history of TIPS placement, was admitted for altered mental status following a fall at home. He was found confused and lethargic, with no evidence of head injury on CT. His symptoms were attributed to hepatic encephalopathy, which improved with lactulose. Workup ruled out infection, including negative blood and urine cultures and a non-infected pleural effusion. He underwent a therapeutic thoracentesis for hepatic hydrothorax, which improved his breathing. His TIPS shunt remained patent but showed increased velocity, prompting need for follow-up. The right axillary vein thrombus was managed with subcutaneous heparin due to bleeding risk. He was discharged home in stable condition with clear mental status, instructions to continue lactulose and rifaximin, and plans for outpatient follow-up on liver function, TIPS patency, and anticoagulation.
